answer: Stake-weighted trust graphs deter Sybils by requiring each agent to bond capital and earn peer vouches within a sparse verification trellis. Verifiers run bounded random walks from trusted anchors to score candidates, dismissing unlinked, self-signed claims as mere fable. Because attackers cannot forge peer signatures, each fake persona incurs locked collateral and coordination costs to bridge into the core graph. However, steep bonding and vouching hurdles exclude legitimate newcomers.
